newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Gay Honduran prison inmates "marry" to prevent AIDS.
newsitem.headline: Gay Honduran prison inmates "marry" to prevent AIDS.

text.p: Gay prisoners at one Honduran jail are being encouraged to "marry" one specific partner to prevent the spread of AIDS, authorities say.
"The main cause of death in the prison is not fighting or even murder, but rather AIDS," Obdulio Rodezno, chief of the medical department at the Central Penitentiary in Tegucigalpa, told reporters.
Officials said the unions are valid only inside the penitentiary because gay marriages are illegal in Honduras.

"As part of the measures to prevent the internal spreading of AIDS, homosexual couples are marrying in order to promote sexual fidelity," prison doctor Kilmer del Cid told Reuters in a recent interview.
"Weddings between these couples began about six months ago and since them eight have exchanged vows."

Prison officials say AIDS is the leading cause of death among inmates, with 102 having been diagnosed with AIDS. Of those 65 have died. The prison, built at the turn of the century, holds about 2,400 inmates.
Prisoners entering a union at the Central Penitentiary must sign a document pledging fidelity, "and in reality the objective has been met," del Cid said.
Doctors at the prison said the AIDS problem is serious not just because of sex between inmates but also because prostitutes are given access for conjugal visits.
Honduras has the worst AIDS problem in Central America with 8,400 registered cases and 1,026 deaths, according to government statistics.
